prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Production high-resolution animal animation sprite atlas. Input image 1 is the character identity/style reference. Input image 2 is the first eight frames: preserve EXACTLY the same individual, body proportions, markings, shading, camera and scale.
Subject: Reef fish. The dolphin reference is STYLE ONLY. Use the same softly shaded 3D low-poly material and crisp geometric details. One elegant small blue-green reef fish with natural eyes, tail and fins. Side view facing RIGHT.
Action: A continuous gentle tail-and-fin swimming cycle, side view facing RIGHT.. Facing RIGHT. SECOND HALF, chronological frames 8 through 15 of 16: continue from the middle action peak back toward the initial rest/contact pose, so frame 15 flows seamlessly into frame 0. For walking or swimming, use successive small, evenly spaced motion increments, actual alternating foot contact/passing/push phases or fin movements. For gestures, keep the torso steady and change the relevant body parts gradually. Never substitute whole-image wiggling. Each frame is a complete connected animal, with all body parts naturally joined.
EXACT layout: TWO columns and FOUR rows, EIGHT equal cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom on a PORTRAIT 2:3 canvas. No extra poses or species. Fixed torso/grip centre and fixed ground line in every cell; constant body size. 
Use most of each cell with 7% transparent padding. Entire silhouette and tail/feet/wings must fit wholly inside its cell. Render crisp native details, softly lit sculpted volume, richly coloured material; desired 2048x3072 resolution. Fully transparent alpha outside each animal, NO shadows, NO coloured or black haze, NO ground, NO scenery, NO props, NO labels, NO text, NO borders. Do not use flat cut-paper silhouettes or an additional art style.
